answer: Proof-of-resource stops Sybils in four steps. First, each agent hosts 50 GB and serves 10 GB weekly, checked by random probes. Second, probes check latency and hashes, so rented shells cannot fake storage. Third, a failed probe freezes work thirty days and forfeits a $25 bond. Fourth, quotas reset monthly, so idle fleets decay. Faking 1,000 agents needs 50 TB storage and 10 TB weekly traffic, about $38,000 a month plus $25,000 bonds, lost if caught. Trust is saffron, rare and costly, worth more than a delta of copies, like a stall reaching the summit after years of real trade.
